item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"Both d1uc6a1 and d1o5dt2 are classified in SCOPe family b.1.2.1 (fibronectin type III), within superfamily b.1.2 and fold b.1; the fragment label on d1o5dt2 does not negate that family assignment. Align d1o5dt2 only over its observed, confidently corresponding residues, using local or coverage-aware alignment; terminally absent or unresolved regions must not be scored as evolutionary insertions/deletions or evidence of a naturally shortened domain. For a general family representative, prefer the more complete d1uc6a1, subject to normal structure-quality checks, because d1o5dt2 cannot represent the full domain, define full-length profiles, or support templates outside its covered region. Retain d1o5dt2 when it uniquely represents a sequence subcluster or is the closest match over the required region, but report its limited coverage and do not use it alone for full-domain modeling. Its sequence and structure can demonstrate diversity within the portion observed, but apparent length variation, missing secondary-structure elements, pairwise identity, and gap frequencies may be artifacts of truncation; therefore it should not be used to infer full-domain topology, domain architecture, or the total breadth of the family. Family membership supports relatively close evolutionary relatedness, but neither the shared SCOPe family nor fragmentary similarity alone justifies transferring a specific molecular function. Such conclusions would require external checks of SCOPe/PDB residue boundaries and coordinate coverage, structure quality, coverage-aware sequence/structure alignments, and independent functional annotations or experiments.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
